news.full_article_text: Alcohol sold in tetra packs may mislead minors, Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response The Supreme Court sought the Centre’s response to a PIL alleging that liquor tetra packs resembling fruit juice could mislead minors, encourage underage drinking and pose health risks. The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought the assistance of solicitor general Tushar Mehta in a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the sale of alcohol in tetra packs, alleging that deceptive packaging resembling fruit juice could mislead consumers, encourage underage drinking and pose public health risks. Granting four weeks for the Centre to file its response to the petition filed by an organisation, Community Against Drunken Driving, a bench headed by justice Vikram Nath said that despite notice being issued on the petition in May, no response had been filed by the Centre, nor had any lawyer appeared on behalf of the central government. “We grant four weeks to the Union of India to file its counter affidavit. In the meantime, the petitioner may serve a copy of the paper book on the office of the solicitor general. List after six weeks,” the bench, also comprising justices R Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh, said. Deep Dive The petition was argued by advocate Vipin Nair, who said, “It seems the Centre is not very serious about the issue.” He said that the packaged alcohol had deceptive names and pictures which attracted minors to consume the drink. “It is alarming that these tetra packs are marketed under labels such as ‘Bunty Premium Vodka’, ‘Chilli Mango Vodka’, and ‘Premium Romanov Vodka – Apple Thrill’, clearly intended to mislead consumers. The use of fruit names alongside colour photographs of apples and mangoes on the packaging further reinforces this deception,” the petition said. The petition was opposed by the Action Alliance for Recycling Beverage Cartons (AARC), a society comprising companies engaged in the packaging business, including those selling alcoholic beverages. An application filed by AARC was argued by senior advocate Arvind Datar, who stated that there was no harm in selling alcoholic beverages in tetra packs and sachets, as such packaging avoids adulteration and cannot be recycled. He further pointed out that such packages are allowed under the prevailing excise laws in 10 states. Datar showed samples of alcoholic beverages and said that health is a state subject and that excise also falls under the jurisdiction of states. The court allowed AARC to be part of the proceedings and granted the association time to file its response to the petition. It also directed the states to respond. Nair said that his petition also seeks mandatory age verification, as the sale of alcohol is prohibited to persons below 18 years of age. The PIL stated that unlike cigarette packs and tobacco sachets, which carry statutory warnings, these packs carry no such labels, and even where warnings are present, they are barely visible. These drinks masquerade as fruit juice, and such packaging facilitates easy access and concealment, encourages underage consumption, promotes public drinking and drunk driving, and even enables smuggling across state borders, it added. The petitioner NGO, which has been actively pursuing a campaign against drunken driving, said that the issue needs to be tackled legally because the definitions of “bottling” and “bottle” under different state excise acts are “broad and varying”, with a bottle encompassing pots, baskets, flasks, wrappers and other similar receptacles. As a result, liquor is available in portable PET bottles, plastic sachets and tetra packs across states. The petition stated that states’ discretion in defining bottles should be guided by environmental and health concerns, rather than solely by the revenue such sales would generate for state coffers. The petition added that the Central Excise law also provides no help in this regard. “It is apparent that the excise authorities in various states have allowed liquor to be packaged and sold in inconspicuous packaging. Such packages are very easy to sneak into public places such as parks, educational institutes, and cinema halls. Even children cannot be spotted easily if they consume liquor from such packages,” the petition said. These packs are cheap, encouraging young, impressionable minds to purchase and consume more, the petition said, urging the court to lay down uniform guidelines to protect the health and lives of citizens.

The petition was opposed by the Action Alliance for Recycling Beverage Cartons (AARC), a society comprising companies engaged in the packaging business, including those selling alcoholic beverages. An application filed by AARC was argued by senior advocate Arvind Datar, who stated that there was no harm in selling alcoholic beverages in tetra packs and sachets, as such packaging avoids adulteration and cannot be recycled. He further pointed out that such packages are allowed under the prevailing excise laws in 10 states. Datar showed samples of alcoholic beverages and said that health is a state subject and that excise also falls under the jurisdiction of states. The court allowed AARC to be part of the proceedings and granted the association time to file its response to the petition. It also directed the states to respond. The petitioner NGO, which has been actively pursuing a campaign against drunken driving, said that the issue needs to be tackled legally because the definitions of “bottling” and “bottle” under different state excise acts are “broad and varying”, with a bottle encompassing pots, baskets, flasks, wrappers and other similar receptacles. news.headline: CEC an institution, not a person, won't enjoy any special privilege: Ex-Supreme Court justice
news.story_lead: CEC an institution, not a person, won't enjoy any special privilege: Ex-Supreme Court justice Justice Joseph invoked concerns raised during the Constituent Assembly debates about the integrity of those responsible for conducting elections. Former Supreme Court judge Justice Kurian Joseph has stressed that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) must not enjoy any special privilege as an individual, arguing that authority should rest with the institution rather than the person holding the office. He called for stronger constitutional safeguards to protect the independence and integrity of the Election Commission of India (ECI).
news.full_article_text: CEC an institution, not a person, won't enjoy any special privilege: Ex-Supreme Court justice Justice Joseph invoked concerns raised during the Constituent Assembly debates about the integrity of those responsible for conducting elections. Former Supreme Court judge Justice Kurian Joseph has stressed that the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) must not enjoy any special privilege as an individual, arguing that authority should rest with the institution rather than the person holding the office. He called for stronger constitutional safeguards to protect the independence and integrity of the Election Commission of India (ECI). “CEC by himself shall not enjoy any special privilege. It is meant to be an institution, not a person. Unfortunately, people holding high constitutional office in our country have, according to me, what they call a misguided impression that there is power concentrated on the person...If it is an institutional exercise of that power, you will have to think twice, he said, as per LiveLaw . Justice Joseph made the remarks while delivering the inaugural address at a seminar titled “Independence of Election Commission of India: Compromised?”, organised by the Indian Association of Lawyers, Keralam. He argued that the appointment of Election Commissioners and the conditions governing their service should be protected through constitutional provisions rather than left to parliamentary legislation. ‘Has democracy been poisoned at its source?’ Justice Joseph invoked concerns raised during the Constituent Assembly debates about the integrity of those responsible for conducting elections. Referring to Constituent Assembly member Hriday Nath Kunzru, he warned that a lack of trust in the officials overseeing elections could undermine democracy itself. “Dr. Hriday Nath Kunzru spoke about the integrity of the person who is holding that office. And if that integrity is not impeccable, then democracy will be poisoned at the source. Is this not what we see in the days that we have been passing through? Has the democracy not been poisoned at the hands of people who have not been acting in accordance with the vision of the Constitution? So, therefore, my dear friends, I would only say these are the times that the country should think about and take steps for protection of our democracy. And if such constitutional powers are vested in great institutions like the Election Commission of India, its integrity and independence should be ensured as well”, he was quoted as saying by Live Law. He maintained that protecting the ECI's independence was essential given the constitutional responsibilities entrusted to it. Justice Joseph seeks safeguards for appointment and removal of Election Commissioners The former judge called for the Constitution to lay down the appointment procedures and service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners. He also proposed that all Election Commissioners should be removable only through the same procedure applicable to Supreme Court judges. Referring to Article 324 of the Constitution, Justice Joseph noted that it gives the ECI superintendence, direction and control over the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections. However, he questioned whether the existing constitutional framework provided sufficient safeguards to ensure the independence of the institution. news.exam_corner_topic: Rahul, Priyanka join Ankita Bhandari's family's protest against ‘VIP’ Sikkim governor's appointment
news.headline: Rahul, Priyanka join Ankita Bhandari's family's protest against ‘VIP’ Sikkim governor's appointment
news.story_lead: Rahul, Priyanka join Ankita Bhandari's family's protest against ‘VIP’ Sikkim governor's appointment Ankita Bhandari, a resident of Uttarakhand, worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Yamkeshwar, near Rishikesh. She was murdered in 2022. Congress leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met the parents of Ankita Bhandari in New Delhi on Wednesday evening.
news.full_article_text: Rahul, Priyanka join Ankita Bhandari's family's protest against ‘VIP’ Sikkim governor's appointment Ankita Bhandari, a resident of Uttarakhand, worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Yamkeshwar, near Rishikesh. She was murdered in 2022. Congress leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met the parents of Ankita Bhandari in New Delhi on Wednesday evening. Together, they staged a sit-in near India Gate against the appointment of former Uttarakhand BJP in-charge Dushyant Kumar Gautam as the Governor of Sikkim. The parents of the 19-year-old receptionist, who was murdered in Uttarakhand’s Pauri Garhwal district in September 2022, have demanded that Gautam’s appointment be put on hold until the ongoing Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged VIP angle in the case was completed. Activist Yogita Bhayana also joined the protest, during which Ankita’s parents requested President Droupadi Murmu to intervene and ensure that the investigation examined all allegations related to the case. Gautam served as the BJP’s Uttarakhand in-charge from November 2020 to August 2026, a period during which the party recorded several electoral victories in the state. He was appointed Sikkim governor on Monday. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi voiced support for Ankita Bhandari’s parents and accused the BJP of protecting a “VIP” accused in the case. On X, Rahul said the family had been waiting for justice for four years, alleging that the accused had instead received protection and a constitutional position. “I and the Congress Party stand with them — in their grief as well as in this fight for justice,” he said. Ankita’s parents demand investigation into alleged VIP role Speaking to the media during the protest, Ankita’s father demanded action against Gautam and called for the statements of actress Urmila Sanawar and former BJP MLA Suresh Rathore to be included in the investigation. “Dushyant Kumar should go to jail...because of the VIP my daughter was murdered,” he told HT. He questioned the progress of the CBI investigation, alleging that it relied on statements made by witnesses in the lower court. He also claimed that the call details of the accused had not been examined. “I request the President not to appoint Dushyant Kumar as governor until the CBI investigation is complete,” he said. “Even though the CBI probe is underway, it is depending on the statements of witnesses in lower court. Statements of Urmila Sanawar and Suresh Rathore should be included in the investigation. The call details of the accused were not examined.” Ankita’s mother also appealed to the President to reconsider the appointment. “We were hurt by the appointment of Kumar as governor. I request the President, who is a woman and will understand my sentiments, to halt the appointment of Kumar as governor,” she said. The family has sought a thorough investigation into the alleged involvement of a VIP in Ankita’s murder. Gautam has not been named as an accused in the cases related to the crime, and the allegations against him remain unproven. Audio clip triggered demands for CBI probe The demand for a fresh investigation into the alleged VIP angle gained momentum after actress Urmila Sanawar, who claims to be the wife of former BJP MLA Suresh Rathore, released an audio clip purportedly containing a telephone conversation between the two. In the recording, Rathore allegedly referred to the involvement of a BJP leader in the case. The clip triggered protests across Uttarakhand, with demonstrators demanding a CBI investigation into the alleged role of the unidentified VIP. Following the protests, the Uttarakhand government ordered a CBI probe in January. Gautam has denied allegations linking him to the murder and filed a case against Rathore, Sanawar, the Uttarakhand unit of the Congress, Uttarakhand Kranti Dal, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and other unidentified individuals over claims connecting him to the case. The Delhi High Court has also directed the removal of social media posts linking Gautam to the murder, observing that the allegations appeared prima facie defamatory, HT reported earlier. Congress protests Gautam’s appointment The protest at India Gate came a day after the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee (UKPCC), led by its president Ganesh Godiyal, held a silent demonstration in Dehradun against Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim governor. The Congress has questioned the decision to appoint Gautam while demands for an investigation into the alleged VIP angle remain unresolved. The party has called for accountability and further scrutiny of the allegations. The Congress accused the BJP-led Centre of protecting Gautam following his appointment as Sikkim governor, alleging that the decision undermined the demand for justice in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case. On X, the party said Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met Ankita’s family at India Gate in New Delhi. “The allegation was that pressure was put on Ankita to provide services to Dushyant Gautam. When Ankita refused, she was murdered,” the Congress alleged. It accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of rewarding Gautam with the gubernatorial appointment despite the allegations against him. “The daughters and women of the country are watching how Narendra Modi and his government are protecting Dushyant Gautam. Instead of delivering justice to Ankita Bhandari, the entire BJP government is bent on silencing the voice of the victim's family,” the Congress wrote. What happened to Ankita Bhandari? Ankita, a resident of Uttarakhand’s Pauri Garhwal district, worked as a receptionist at Vanantra Resort in Yamkeshwar, near Rishikesh. She was murdered on September 18, 2022. The resort’s owner, Pulkit Arya, son of expelled BJP leader Vinod Arya, and his two employees, Saurabh Bhaskar and Ankit Gupta, were convicted in the case. The three men allegedly pushed Ankita into the Chilla canal following a dispute. A court in Kotdwar, Pauri Garhwal district, sentenced all three accused to life imprisonment in May 2025. The alleged involvement of an unidentified VIP remains a contentious issue. - Priyanka Gandhi Vadra
